A rate of 0 over a denominator of 770 would have read as leg 3's decisive "near zero in real gameplay" outcome and closed the issue on where the bracket sat. Arm B for v2 is e353735028, which wraps the whole of begin_pre_draw so that the consume and the upload that reads guest memory are in one window. v1's two arm-B runs are retained as the negative control for the placement, not discarded.

WHY v2 EXISTS, REASON 2 -- v1's COST STATISTIC MEASURES PHASE ALIGNMENT, NOT COST. v1 declared p90 gfps and p10 G ms and was right to fix a statistic in advance; the statistic itself is wrong for this title. This is the same trap as the median-is-occupancy warning one level down: a percentile of a non-stationary series is a measurement of the series' shape.

LEG 6 RESTATED, and the statistic is fixed HERE, before any e353735028 number exists.
  primary: THE NUMBER OF hakuX-perf gfps LINES IN A FIXED 150 s SOAK. The line fires once per 60 guest frames, so this is guest frames rendered in fixed wall time, divided by 60 -- a single monotone scalar, phase-insensitive, and exactly the throughput the cost question asks about. DOA3 arm B on the buggy ref gave 58 lines = ~3,480 guest frames in 150 s.
  secondary, reported with the caveat above and NOT part of the verdict: p90 gfps, p10 G ms, and median gfps (occupancy).

  expected: below the floor. The corrected probe scans only when texture_vram_gen bumped across a window, which the buggy run measures at 770 of 446,892 windows, so the common path is one 32-bit compare per draw. The vertex site scans once per vertex-range copy, 32,847 of them in 150 s. But "read-only" is a claim about a bitmap's implementation and not a measurement, which is why this leg exists at all.

THE INSTRUMENT, as it now stands. Two device-thread reads of d->vram_ptr, each preceded by a test-and-CLEAR of the very dirty bits it then scans, which is what turns "written at some point since boot" into a WINDOW:
  Vr:raced/copies          sync_vertex_ram_buffer test-and-clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a range and then copies it out of guest memory. Clean on entry by construction; a bit set again when the copy returns is a guest store into it DURING the copy.
  Tr:raced/uploads/windows begin_pre_draw windows. pgraph_vk_poll_bound_textures consumes every bound texture's DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX bits at the top of the window and bumps texture_vram_gen when it finds any, so a bump means the guest had written a bound texture and we then read that memory; `raced` means the bits were set again by the time the window closed.
  Xd:                      the impossible row, leg 1.
No write side, deliberately: a per-page last-written stamp would be a store in every guest VRAM write, the position the +34.1% instrumentation occupied.

ARMS. A = 13ccda425a (integration branch HEAD, no probe). B = e353735028 (A plus the probe, nothing else). Title and device held fixed: Dead or Alive 3 on the THOR for the cost pair, whose attract loop renders real gameplay without needing input injection. Crimson Skies on the THOR as a second reading, because its attract FMV is per-frame dynamic VRAM traffic -- the workload #54 itself names as the one the test corpus cannot exercise. One --who across all of them so device_label cannot drift, which is how #64's cost leg lost its control.

LEG 1 -- THE IMPOSSIBLE ROW. Xd reads EXACTLY 0 on every run of arm B.
Xd counts a dirty bit observed to go from set to clear between two back-to-back scans of the same range with nothing between them but the probe's own arithmetic. The guest only ever SETS these bits, and the only code in this process that clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A or _NV2A_TEX is the vertex sync and check_texture_dirty, both on the thread already inside the call. The arithmetic forbids it.
The worlds in which it FAILS, none forced by the patch: page indices that straddle a DIRTY_MEMORY_BLOCK_SIZE boundary wrongly, so the second scan reads a different word than the first; an RCU blocks pointer that is not stable across a scan; or the pfifo and pgraph.vk.render threads running these paths concurrently after all -- render_thread.c's RCMD_FLUSH does call pgraph_vk_update_vertex_ram_buffer, and this probe assumes the requester waits on flush_complete. A non-zero Xd indicts the instrument, not the emulator, and every other leg is void until it is explained. (It read 0 on both v1 runs, over 446,892 windows and 32,847 copies, which is evidence for the arithmetic but not for the new window.)

LEG 2 -- THE PATH IS LIVE. tex_windows > 0, tex_uploads > 0 AND vtx_copies > 0 on every run of arm B.
v1 satisfies the first and third already. tex_uploads is the one that matters now: it was 770 under the wrong bracket and must be far larger under the right one, because the poll bumps the gen on every draw where a bound texture was written. A tex_uploads still in the hundreds means the window is still in the wrong place and leg 3 is not measured. Predicted tex_uploads > 5,000 per 150 s soak.
A zero or near-zero denominator reads as "not measured", never as "zero races" -- that is the failure that once made a patch measure 0 better and 0 worse because the device took a different path.

LEG 3 -- THE RATE, which is the measurement #54 needs.
Predicted: 1e-4 <= Tr/tex_uploads <= 3e-1 on Dead or Alive 3.
Not fitted from anything this arm produces. The lower bound is a claim that the window is hit at all in a game; the upper is set by #44, where the same race in a synthetic tight loop loses on 1 to 3 of 12 testifying swatches per run over 6 of 10 runs -- order 10% per upload under maximal pressure -- and a game re-binds far more textures than it re-uploads, so the game rate must sit below that.
The two decisive outcomes, declared before the number exists:
  Tr/tex_uploads effectively zero (< 1e-4, and Tr == 0 on every run, with leg 2 passing so the denominator is real) -> the window is never hit in practice, the hazard is theoretical, and #54 CLOSES on evidence rather than on argument. This is the outcome #54's own text predicts under "incidental ordering elsewhere -- locks, syscalls, the PFIFO path itself -- may serialise enough in practice that the window is never hit."
  Tr/tex_uploads >= 1e-4 -> #54 gains a frequency, a call-site list and a target. It does NOT gain a licence for the blanket barrier: the +34.1% experiment already localised that cost to TCG code generation (renderer idle 27 -> 44 ms while frame time went 52 -> 70 ms), so the answer is targeted fences at the few sites a device thread reads guest memory.
The failing world: the guest genuinely never writes a bound texture's page while the upload is reading it, because the pushbuffer handshake serialises them. Real, and nothing in this patch forces it either way -- the probe reads a bitmap the memory subsystem maintains whether the probe exists or not.

LEG 4 -- THE TEXTURE SITE RACES MORE THAN THE VERTEX SITE.
Predicted: Vr/vtx_copies < Tr/tex_uploads.
Mechanism: the vertex window is a memcpy of a few KB; the texture window is a poll, a convert, a swizzle and a staging copy of up to megabytes -- one to three orders of magnitude longer, and a race rate scales with the window.
The failing world is concrete: a title streaming dynamic vertex buffers rewrites them immediately before drawing from them far more often than it rewrites textures, which inverts the ordering. An inversion changes the target list for a narrow fix, and is a finding rather than a refutation.

LEG 5 -- WHETHER THE SAME INSTRUMENT MEASURES #44's SKEW.
Tr counts "a bound texture's dirty bits were consumed inside the window and set again by the time it closed", which is the guest writing the texture while the upload read it -- #44's resolved mechanism, the upload for draw N reading guest memory after the guest has begun writing iteration N+1 to the same address.
Predicted: Tr > 0 on at least one arm-B run.
The limit, stated in advance so it is not read into the result later. Tr is a FLOOR on #44's skew rate: if the guest COMPLETES iteration N+1's write before the poll clears the bits, the clear consumes that write, the upload reads a fully written successor, and nothing is set again -- #44's `cut == complete` case, invisible here. No barrier can fix reading the wrong version of a completed write, and no read-side counter can see it either. Page granularity cuts the other way: a write to the same 4 KiB page but a different byte counts, so Tr is an UPPER bound on byte-level overlap. Floor on version skew, ceiling on byte overlap; different quantities, and neither is "the rate at which frames are corrupted".
This lane does not touch pacing. nv2a.c and pfifo.c belong to the skew lane; any overlap is reported to it rather than acted on.

CONTROLS, not legs.
  mb_emitted must read 0 on the hakuX-build line in BOTH arms. Neither arm restores barriers; a non-zero value means the wrong ref was built. (v1: 0, as required.)
  Tq: (tex_dirty_queries) must be indistinguishable between the arms. The probe adds no test-and-clear and removes none, so if Tq moves, the probe has changed the path it is observing. (v1 arm B: median 629.)
  device_label must read "thor" on every result. Four soaks across two handhelds with nothing recording which is how #64's cost leg lost its control.
  apk_sha must differ between the arms and agree within each arm.

ASSERTIONS, recorded so they are not counted as falsifiers, because the code forces them: Tr <= tex_uploads <= tex_windows, and Vr <= vtx_copies.

WHAT THIS ARM CANNOT DECIDE. Whether a race it counts actually corrupted a frame. It counts windows, not wrong pixels, and a soak has no frame capture -- an exclusion already established on #54 which this instrument does not lift. It also cannot see the surface-upload read, deliberately uninstrumented: nothing on the device clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a surface range -- the vertex sync clears only its own ranges and update_surface_part's own scan is behind !tcg_enabled() -- so the bitmap is monotone there and a probe on it would report a plausible number with no time base in it.

FORM. ab_compare's machine-readable slots are per-capture and a soak produces no captures, so the registered expect_counts are degenerate on purpose (better=0, worse=0, must_not_move '*' -- if ANY capture appears in either arm the request was mis-dispatched as a suites run and every leg here is void). The legs are numbers read off the hakuX-perf line by docs/testing/vram_race_report.py; they are bound here by this file's content hash, which is the point of registering before the device runs.
